````text
# #4743: Patch: a play still being built closes when the game ends on your turn, instead of covering the result
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

In an online game you can be halfway through a play on your own turn: you clicked a card in your hand and its "Choose a target" or "Choose Tributes" window is open, or you are dragging a Unit onto an enemy. If the game ends at that moment without you doing anything (your opponent concedes, runs out of reconnect time, or accepts the draw you offered), the board shows the game is over, but that window stays open, drawn on top of the Victory panel with the board dimmed under it. Picking an option in it sends a play to a game that is already over, and letting go of the drag sends the attack; only Cancel clears it.

Once this is built, the game ending drops whatever you were still building, as the turn ending already does, and the result panel is the only thing on screen. Players of online, daily and co-op games see it, most often when an opponent concedes the moment they see the lethal coming.

## Why

- `apps/web/src/game/Game.tsx:830-839` drops a half-built play or attack (#2924) only when `boardKeyOf(shown)` changes, and `apps/web/src/game/actions.ts:107-109` makes that key `turn:active:viewer`. A game that ends on the viewer's own turn through no action of theirs (the opponent's `concede`, R211; `disconnect`; `draw-accepted`; `match-ceiling`, all `GameOverReason`s) changes none of the three, so the `interaction` survives into the finished game. Nothing else in `Game.tsx` resets it on `result`; the player's own concede is fine only because `confirmConcede` goes through `dispatch`, which sets `IDLE` (`Game.tsx:754-766`, `858-864`).
- `Game.tsx:1088-1106` mounts `<Prompt>` whenever `promptOver` is false (`game/promptOver.ts:13-21`), which never reads `result`. With `pending` null once the game is over (`docs/implicit-states.md` E7), `Prompt.tsx:2025-2041` builds the play's own picker from `interaction` alone (`outstandingNeed`), never reading `legal`.
- The picker covers the result: `.prompt-scrim` is at `--z-modal` (40; `game/prompt.css:23-30`, `surfaces.css:35-36`), the result overlay and its scrim at `--z-showcase` (39; `game/animations.css:1746-1751`, `1883-1888`), both centred. The overlay's comment puts it "below the prompt scrim" on purpose, which is right for an engine prompt (never open after the end, E7) but not for a play's own picker.
- A drag in flight has the same hole: `game/drag/DragLayer.tsx:391-398` ends a flight without sending only when `movedOn` (`:262-264`, #3899's G7 fix) sees the newest view's `boardKeyOf` differ from the one it was lifted on. Otherwise `resolveDrop` (`game/drag/model.ts:281-292`) resolves the drop from the build it was lifted with, so a release after a same-turn end sends that attack or play, which the finished game refuses (R216). A click with an attacker still selected takes the same `onClickTarget` path.
- `docs/implicit-states.md` section 6 lists the board's combinations G1 to G24. G5 (a selection, then another turn) and G7 (a flight, then another turn) drop the build; no row covers a selection or a flight when the game ends on the same turn.
- Every live board is this `Game`, and none remounts it on a result: `routes/match.tsx:504`, `daily/DailyBoard.tsx`, `duos/DuosBoard.tsx`.

## Proposal

Make the game's end part of the key #2924 drops a build on: `boardKeyOf` returns `turn:active:viewer` plus a mark when `view.result !== null` (for example a trailing `:over`). The existing adjust-state-while-rendering drop in `Game.tsx` then closes the picker and clears a selected attacker on the render that shows the result, and `DragLayer`'s `movedOn` ends a flight lifted before the end without sending anything. No CSS or z-index change; engine prompts, replays (no drag layer, read-only prompts) and the same-turn behaviour G4, G6, G8 and G15 pin are untouched.

Rejected alternative: not mounting `<Prompt>` once `shown.result !== null`. It closes the picker but leaves `interaction` set, so a drag's release or a click still sends, and it adds a second rule beside #2924's.

## Where it lands

- `apps/web/src/game/actions.ts`: `boardKeyOf` and its comment.
- `apps/web/src/game/Game.test.tsx`: the block "a half-built play or attack is dropped at the turn change (#2924)".
- `apps/web/src/test/ux/drag-layer.test.tsx`: "layer states 3899".
- `docs/implicit-states.md` section 6: a row G25 (a selection or a flight, then the game ends on the same turn), and "G1 to G24" becomes "G1 to G25".
- SPEC section 2.5 (nothing happens after the game is over, R216); R211 (concede is always on offer).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test in `Game.test.tsx`: on the viewer's turn, a hand card with two plays opens its picker (`data-prompt-source="play"`); rerendering the same turn, seat and viewer with a `result` (reason `concede`) and `legal=[]` leaves no `prompt-scrim`. It fails on `main`.
- [ ] A test in the same block: a selected attacker is dropped when a same-turn view with a `result` arrives, and a click on its old target sends nothing.
- [ ] A test in `drag-layer.test.tsx`: a flight lifted on the viewer's turn, then a same-turn view with a `result`, then a release over the target it was lifted for, never calls `onAction`. It fails on `main`.
- [ ] The existing #2924 and #3899 tests (G4 "keeps the selected attacker through view updates within the same turn" among them) pass unchanged.
- [ ] `docs/implicit-states.md` section 6 has a G25 row naming the new tests.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/Game.test.tsx src/test/ux/drag-layer.test.tsx`, `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and `pnpm exec eslint apps/web` pass.

## Size and risks

Small, medium difficulty: one line of behaviour in `actions.ts`, two or three tests, one table row. `boardKeyOf` has two readers (`Game.tsx:835`, `DragLayer.tsx:263` and `:383`), and both should drop a build at the game's end, so the wider key changes nothing else. A result that lands inside a burst is keyed on `shown`, as G5b is, so the build drops once the board shows the finished game, not while the last animation plays. No ruling: like #2924's drop at the turn change, this is presentation (CLAUDE.md rule 7), and the engine already refuses every action after the end (R216).
